title: Graphing a Scaled and Shifted Reciprocal Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = 1 / (2x) - 1 by starting with the standard reciprocal graph y = 1 / x and applying appropriate transformations.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \frac{1}{x} \text{ compressed vertically by } 2 \text{ and shifted down } 1;\quad \text{VA: } x = 0,\quad \text{HA: } y = -1,\quad \text{x-intercept: } \left(\frac{1}{2}, 0\right)

steps.title: Identify the Scaling and Vertical Shift from y = 1/x
steps.explanation: Start with the hyperbola y = 1/x, compress it vertically by a factor of 2 (or compress horizontally by a factor of 2) to get y = 1/(2x), and shift it down 1 unit to get y = 1/(2x) - 1.
steps.why: Multiplying 1/x by 1/2 scales vertically by 1/2, and subtracting 1 translates downward by 1.

steps.title: Determine the Asymptotes, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The vertical asymptote remains x = 0, while the horizontal asymptote shifts from y = 0 down to y = -1.

steps.title: Locate the x-Intercept and Guide Points
steps.explanation: The right branch passes through (1/2, 0) and (1, -1/2); the left branch lies in the third quadrant passing through (-1/2, -2) and (-1, -3/2).
steps.why: Solving 1/(2x) = 1 yields the unique x-intercept x = 1/2.
